Subject: Redwood VPC — ask on packaging and credits

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — team appreciated the performance numbers. We're beginning to budget for a private VPC deployment and need a clearer commercial picture before we take this to procurement. Two asks: 1) a split of the upfront platform fee vs. the recurring licensing/instance commit (we'd like to understand amortization options over 24/36 months), and 2) clarity on support tiers and what is included at each level (response times, on-call routing, and optional SRE add-on).

Also — are there standard credit plays you offer for migrations (e.g., onboarding credits or first-quarter unit credits) if we commit to a 3-year term? We're evaluating a couple of vendors and want to compare total cost of ownership with a realistic ramp.

Appreciate a short commercial note and any attached scenarios we can share internally.

Best,

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear asks.

TL;DR: We can offer a modular commercial structure with an amortizable platform fee, optional SRE add-on, and graduated onboarding credits tied to commit length. I attached three scenarios (24/36/48 months) with sample amortization and net-effective unit rates.

What's included (short):
- Platform fee: one-time, customer-visible line that covers private control plane, managed deployment automation, and initial security onboarding. Can be amortized across the term; default amortization period we quote is 36 months.
- Licensing / committed capacity: metered GPU units or reserved instance-equivalents billed monthly against the commit.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours SLAs, email + ticket triage), Premium (24x7 response target, prioritized on-call, regular QBRs), SRE Ops (dedicated SRE hours for runbook run-throughs and escalation support).
- Onboarding credits: we propose a tiered credit schedule (3% of first-year committed spend for 24m, 5% for 36m, 7% for 48m) applied as token credits in month 1-3.

I've looped in Karthik and Aditya for the SOW and technical packaging notes — Karthik, can you confirm how we present the on-prem packaging options and the SRE hourly blocks? Aditya, can you attach the pricing scenarios workbook referenced above?

Next steps: I'll share a concise commercial one-pager + scenario workbook and can set a 30-min call with procurement next week. Does Tues 7/7 at 10am PT work for you?

Regards,

Hi all — quick technical/commercial notes to include in the one-pager:

1) Packaging options (present as three SKU families):
   - "Core VPC": private control plane + standard runtime containers, intended for teams that self-manage day-to-day ops. Includes 90 days of onboarding runbooks and one workshop.
   - "Managed VPC": Core VPC + deployment automation, patching, and monthly health checks. Includes the Premium support band.
   - "SRE-backed VPC": Managed VPC + dedicated SRE hours (blocks sold in 100-hr increments) and custom runbook ownership.

2) SRE pricing guidance:
   - Block pricing: $18k per 100-hr block (volume discount at 300+ hrs).
   - Alternatively, dedicated fractional SRE allocation for long-term customers priced as a recurring SKU.

3) Platform fee amortization examples (from workbook):
   - Example A (36m): $360k platform fee -> $10k/mo amortized; combined with committed units yields net-effective per-token/unit rate shown in workbook.
   - We can split the platform fee across service lines if procurement requires separate CAPEX/OPEX accounting — we have precedent with two customers where we split 60/40 across initial platform + ops retainer.

4) Credits & migration concessions:
   - Standard: onboarding credits (applied as token credits) tied to term length as Vanessa proposed.
   - For accelerated signature (sign by EOM), we can add a one-time implementation credit equal to one 100-hr SRE block as a professional services credit.

If this reads OK I can help draft the SOW appendix that maps SKUs to billing codes.

—Karthik

1) Can you provide a net-effective pricing table that shows the first-year blended unit cost after onboarding credits and proposed amortization? We need a single line to compare against the incumbent.

If possible, could you turn these into a short redlineable term sheet so legal/procurement can react quickly? We're aiming to complete vendor selection by 7/15.

Ellen

Hi Ellen — thanks, and great timing on the 7/15 procurement target. Below is a concise response to each procurement ask and a suggested next step (I'll attach a redline-friendly term sheet after you confirm).

1) Net-effective first-year blended table: we've added a "Net-Effective" tab to the workbook (Redwood_VPC_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx) which shows three columns — list rates, onboarding credit applied (per term), and resulting first-year blended unit rate. For your scenario at 250 units, 36m, Premium + one 100-hr SRE block, your blended cost reduces by ~4.2% after the onboarding credit. I'll export a single-page PDF of that table and attach.

2) All-in uplift for Premium + 100-hr SRE: Rough guidance — Premium support adds ~12% to licensing spend; a 100-hr SRE block is $18k one-time (as Karthik noted). For your 250-unit case we estimate the all-in uplift to be in the low-to-mid teens percentage-wise versus base commit. Exact dollar delta is in the workbook.

3) Platform fee discount: We're willing to offer a one-time 15% platform fee discount in exchange for a 36-month committed term and a customer case-study agreement (standard carve-outs for PHI/PII kept). We can improve to 20% contingent on an accelerated contract signature (within 14 days of the final SOW).

Next step: If that framework looks good, I'll prepare the redlineable term sheet + a single-page commercial summary and target a procurement call on 7/10 at 10am PT to walk through line-by-line. Please confirm preferred time and whether your procurement needs any additional paperwork (tax forms, PO templates).

Thanks — excited to get this over the line.
